review_type: AI Agent independent evidence review (not human/blind)
scope: Review of existing local evidence and code; no model/network rerun; only independent-review.json created.
method_notes: run.py uses real create_client(settings) and DiagnosisService.diagnose_detail, asserts non-Mock, creates a fresh service per case, and does not call the resume parser or modify prompts.
Both inputs are fixed before the loop. Started status is persisted before invocation; all non-pending cases are skipped; failures are retained without fabricated results.

Client callbacks record error status in finally. DiagnosisService retries TemporaryLLMError up to max_attempts with 1s then 2s backoff. Durations support three approximately 30s attempts plus 3s backoff per case.
Two outer case invocations and six internal requests are supported by records and runner control flow. They are not six evaluation cases.
Current configuration/endpoint/prompt hashes match the supplemental frozen record. The original fixed evaluation also records glm-5.2 and openai_chat.

limitations.description: Neither case obtained successful STAR output; all four quality dimensions remain null.
TemporaryLLMError covers timeout, connection failure, and retryable HTTP failure; recorded attempts omit underlying error details. Precise network root cause cannot be determined.

Original fixed operator record lacks full configuration and endpoint/prompt hash, so equality of all settings to that earlier run cannot be independently proven; current and supplemental frozen configuration equality is verified.

Local source provenance and record consistency do not establish truth of source authors claims, external provider receipt, or completeness of historical invocations. This review is AI evidence review, not human/blind quality evaluation.

Archived TeX files use CRLF in this checkout. Their raw byte hashes differ from recorded source_sha256, but LF normalization and HEAD Git blob hashes match exactly for both. No source content change was found.

report_consistency_review.result: Consistent with recorded two failed case invocations and six internal error attempts. Both reports explicitly distinguish request failure from a successful empty STAR result, prohibit quality scoring, and preserve the original evaluation denominator.
